review_id: # The review record (framework 1.1.0). One row per human review of the deliverable.
# Copy this file into the analysis directory as `review-record.tsv`.
# WHY THIS FILE EXISTS
#   "A human reviewed it" is a claim about a process, and until now nothing recorded the
#   process. Tier 2 spent human time and produced a signature. This file makes the review
#   a measurable component instead of a ceremony: its duration, the disagreements it
#   surfaced, what it overrode, and what it caught.
# scope        : comma-separated claim_id / step_id this review covered. A review that
#                does not say what it covered cannot be said to have covered anything —
#                the checker requires every human-verified claim at tier 2 to appear in
#                some record's scope.
# reviewer     : the same identity rule as the claim ledger — a personal name, initials,
#                or a stable handle / role id (@wuwei, lab-lead, pi). Empty or a
#                placeholder is a FAIL: it is indistinguishable from nobody looking.
# duration_min : positive number of minutes. A review with no time attached cannot be
#                told apart from a glance at the summary.
# disagreements / overrides : how many conclusions the reviewer disputed / overturned.
# disagreements_detail      : required whenever disagreements > 0.
# errors_found : integer >= 0. 0 is a legal and informative value — it is not the same
#                as blank, and blank is a FAIL because the two cannot be told apart.
# error_classes_found : the `class` / `emergent_kind` values from error-ledger.tsv that
#                this review surfaced. `-` when none.
# verdicts_changed : how many claim levels changed after the review.
# calibration_note : one line on what this review's outcome says about the review process
#                itself (too shallow? found the load-bearing error? mostly cosmetic?).
# The checker reports the totals across records (count, mean duration, overrides, errors
# found) and sets no threshold on them. A numeric quota would convert a measurement into
# a paperwork target, which is how a gate stops being read.
# One judgement rule that is deliberately NOT automated (SKILL.md): if tier-2 reviews
# return errors_found = 0 several times running, the signal is about the review process,
# not about the analysis. A gate that costs human time and never catches anything should
# be simplified or redesigned — not multiplied.
